overview: A poem about mentorship, loss, and carrying forward the legacy of a great teacher. Inspired by Parashat Tetzaveh, which is the only parsha from Shemot to Devarim that does not directly mention Moses's name. The key lies in his absence — in our most daring moments, our greatest mentors will not be with us physically, but if they did a great job they will always be with us spiritually. Dedicated to our best mentors and teachers.
poem_lines: The ground of his almond tree was watered with tears.
with her poppy flowers in bloom,
note that the student had to read
As he read the touching songs
poem_hebrew_lines: אדמת עץ השקד שלו הושקתה בדמעות.
